title: Invite risk scoring and automated remediation for org/team joins
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a risk-scoring layer to the invite pipeline and wire automated remediation actions (quarantine, require manager approval, auto-block domain) tied into RBAC v2 defaults and enriched audit logging. The goal is to reduce successful high-risk joins while preserving low-friction invites for trusted orgs and SSO-verified domains. This ticket covers scoring design, audit schema changes, rule engine, feature flags, rollout strategy, and instrumentation for metrics and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Risk score is computed for every outgoing invite and persisted to invites table and audit log
Automated remediation actions trigger based on configurable thresholds and are reversible by admins
RBAC v2 onboarding rules apply role defaults based on risk band (low/medium/high)
Audit logs are enriched with invite metadata including risk_score, domain_reputation, sso_verified, inviter_ip_geo
Feature flags allow gradual rollout and emergency disable (invite_risk_v1, invite_auto_remediate)
Dashboard shows invites_by_risk, blocked_invites, time_to_resolve escalations, and false_positive rate
E2E tests for SAML/SSO, allowlist/denylist exception paths, and manual approval flow exist and pass in CI
implementation_notes: Scoring model: weighted sum of signals with normalized weights: domain_reputation (0.35), sso_domain_verified (0.25 negative weight), inviter_history_score (0.15), invite_acceptance_rate_by_domain (0.10), ip_geolocation_anomaly (0.10), role_targeted_sensitivity (0.05)
Domain reputation uses external vendor + internal denylist; values mapped to 0-100. SSO_verified reduces score by fixed delta but cannot below 0.

Remediation actions: allow (auto-accept), require_manager_approval (invite in pending queue), quarantine (invite unexpanded, notification to security), auto_block_domain (requires security opt-in / audit trail)
RBAC v2 integration: new onboarding preset 'risk_aware_default' that maps risk bands to roles: low->member, medium->limited_member, high->guest/pending. This is configurable per-org via Console.

Audit log schema additions: invite_id, risk_score, risk_signals (as comma-separated tags), domain_reputation_score, sso_verified, inviter_ip_geo (country/city), action_taken, operator_id, event_timestamp, audit_event_id
Feature flags: invite_risk_v1 (compute & log only), invite_auto_remediate (enable automated actions), invite_ui_warnings (show warnings in Console)

test_plan: Unit: scoring function boundary tests and individual signal mocks
Integration: end-to-end invite flow with SAML provider; ensure sso_verified lowers score
E2E: Console flow where admin sees warning, can approve or deny; manual approval triggers audit event
Chaos: toggle feature flags mid-invite to validate idempotency and rollback behavior
Load: simulate 10k invites/hour to validate scoring service latency (target <50ms per invite scoring)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (flag=invite_risk_v1): compute and log scores for all invites only; no user-facing impact. Monitor metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (flag=invite_ui_warnings): surface warnings in Console for medium/high invites; add manager-approval workflow as manual opt-in for 5% of orgs
Phase 3 (flag=invite_auto_remediate): enable automated remediation for internal enterprise orgs with security approval; keep auto_block_domain disabled by default
Phase 4: broaden to self-serve orgs and enable RBAC v2 onboarding presets as default for new orgs; provide opt-out for privacy-sensitive customers
risks_and_mitigations: False positives: mitigate by gradual rollout, allow appeal flow, and threshold tuning using labeled historical data
Privacy concerns: store only signal summaries in audit log and respect org retention settings; provide opt-out for certain customers
Operational overhead: queue for manager approvals could grow; add SLA and escalation to security queue and rate-limit auto-remediation
SSO bypass risk: ensure SAML assertion validation and prefer SSO_verified flag only when assertion contains domain match and verifier check succeeds
